item.title: Zeus 0.3.3
item.description:
Calmer, safer and more reliable

Fixes

  • Handed-over work no longer leaves Zeus waiting. When your assistant hands you something with actions such as "Looks good" or "Revise", Zeus no longer treats it as an unanswered question. The avatar doesn't sit in its waiting pose, and assistant updates and new instructions aren't held back while such a card is open. Replying in the chat closes the actions, and a newer version of the same item replaces them.
  • Unread means unread. Cards your assistant withdrew, or that expired, no longer count as unread or make Zeus look like it wants your attention.
  • Restart Assistant waits for a good moment. Restarting no longer interrupts your assistant mid-task or throws away text you've typed in its Terminal. Zeus restarts it once it's idle, and you can cancel while it waits. If the assistant is stuck or has stopped, Restart Now is offered, with a warning.
  • The menu shows its questions. If Restart Assistant needs you to confirm something, such as a pending switch to another assistant, Zeus now opens Settings at that question instead of doing nothing.
  • OpenCode recovers after Zeus restarts. If Zeus quits while sending a message to OpenCode, it finishes sending it when it starts again, so later messages don't get stuck behind it.

item.title: Zeus 0.3.2
item.description:
Your assistant keeps its plans across restarts

Fixes

  • Restarts no longer silently cancel your assistant's checks. Your assistant sets its own timers for things like its next check-in, and those timers end whenever it restarts, for example after a Zeus update or Restart Assistant. Zeus now tells your assistant when it has been restarted and why, so it can set its plans again. Nothing is sent when a new conversation starts.

item.title: Zeus 0.3.1
item.description:
Your assistant's rules work with app names

Fixes

  • Rules can name apps. When your assistant proposes a rule like "hold routine cards while Logic Pro is in front," Zeus now finds the app by its name. Before, Zeus accepted only internal app IDs, so a rule that named an app was rejected.
  • Good rules aren't lost. If your assistant proposes several rules and one has a problem, Zeus keeps the others and tells the assistant exactly which rule and which part to fix. Before, one problem threw out every rule in the request, with an error that didn't say what was wrong.

item.title: Zeus 0.3.0
item.description:
Your assistant works ahead for you

  • Morning brief. At the start of your day, Zeus asks your assistant for one short brief: what's coming up, what's at risk and what it has ready. It uses what it knows about you, its own notes and its own tools, such as calendar, mail and tasks, if it has them. If nothing matters, it stays quiet. It works even with Learn from me off. Turn it on or off in Settings › Morning brief, or rate "Morning brief" messages like any other kind.
  • It prepares, not just waits. When Zeus tells your assistant something new, the assistant now asks itself whether anything needs preparing or flagging. If so, it does the work and tells you in one short message. Otherwise it stays quiet.
  • Rules that act now fire. When a rule's moment comes, Zeus tells your assistant, so a rule you approved can act, and a rule still waiting for your OK shows you what it would have done.
  • A daily limit on unprompted messages. After six unprompted messages in a day, more arrive collapsed with Show. Urgent messages always come through.

It learns you, not just your last hour

  • Evening reflection from weeks of patterns. The reflection is now a summary of the last four weeks, built on your Mac: when you usually start and wind down, what you work on at which times, things you do in the same order, recurring topics, and which of your assistant's messages you use. It's no longer a list of today's app switches. Your assistant updates its notes about you (Notes/about-you.md, Notes/patterns.md), suggests rules only for patterns that held over several days, and gets ready for tomorrow.
  • Reflections and briefs actually arrive. Long deliveries reach your assistant as a short line it follows to fetch the full text. Before, they could sit in the queue whenever its Terminal window was too small to check them.
  • Restart Assistant picks up the new instructions (v7) if you haven't edited your copy.

Fixes

  • Back to where you were. Coming back from a document now returns the conversation to the same spot, however you go back, even after expanding the viewer, stepping between attachments or getting new messages. Before, it jumped to the top.
  • No leftover attachments. If typing or quoting attached the document to your message and you then clear the message, the document is no longer attached. A document you attach on purpose with Ask About This stays.
  • Back to the right message from the speech bubble. If you open a document from the speech bubble and then go back, the conversation now shows the message it came from instead of the oldest history.
  • Your files are safe in a shared folder. If your assistant's folder already had a Zeus folder of your own, Delete Everything could remove files Zeus never wrote, and Zeus's first save there could overwrite one of yours with the same name. Zeus now deletes and replaces only files it wrote itself. If one of your files is where Zeus wants to write, Zeus leaves it alone and Settings tells you which file it is.
  • Links within a document work. A link to a heading in the same document scrolls to it instead of opening the document again. A link to a heading in another file opens that file at the heading.
  • Stepping between attachments skips what can't be shown. ‹ › no longer counts apps, scripts or missing files, so it never looks enabled when it can't move.
  • Your daily summary keeps its facts. In your assistant's folder, the daily summary and notes had times and durations replaced with placeholders such as ‹name›, so your assistant couldn't learn your hours from them. They now match what Zeus sent, and existing files are repaired on the next save.
  • Universal Control isn't an app. Time with your cursor on another Mac or iPad is now shown as "On another device" instead of being counted as your top app.
  • Steadier document previews. Zeus now closes a Quick Look preview only once, which prevents a crash found in testing.
  • App names stay app names. Zeus sometimes hid an app name such as "Warp" as if it were a person or a secret in its screen and typing records, so your assistant couldn't tell which app you were working in. App names and other details from macOS now stay intact, older records get their app names back where Zeus can look them up, and what you typed or saw is still redacted.
  • Typing topics say what you were working on. Most typing topics came out as "Drafting in Warp" because one unrecognized recipient, such as an AI assistant, made Zeus discard the whole topic. Topics now describe the subject, such as "Guitar arrangement feedback", and names, numbers and secrets are still kept out.
  • Every learning item shows what happened to it. If a newer brief or reflection replaces one that wasn't sent, or one expires, the conversation now says so instead of still saying it's ready. What Zeus Kept lists those items under a new "Not sent" group for seven days.
  • One name for each kind. Morning summary, Evening reflection, Morning brief request, Note, Rule trigger and Message preference are now called the same thing everywhere. A long item such as a reflection opens in the document viewer instead of filling the conversation.
  • Settings list everything Zeus sends. Settings › Privacy has a new "What Zeus sends your assistant" section that names each kind, when it's sent and which switch controls it. That includes the evening reflection and the morning brief request, which goes even when Learn from me is off. Settings that do nothing while learning is off are now disabled.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.9
item.description:
• Read documents right in the conversation. Click a file your assistant attached, and the panel slides over to a document viewer. ← Messages (Esc or ⌘[) takes you back to exactly where you were.
  • Open it your way. The viewer's header has Open in (⌘O), Show in Finder (⌘⇧R), and a menu with Copy Path and Open With.
  • Room to read. The viewer opens at the chat's size. Expand grows it to a reading size, and Collapse shrinks it back.
  • Every kind of file.
    • Markdown is shown formatted, with a Source toggle for the raw text.
    • Text and code appear in a monospaced font.
    • Images and PDFs are shown directly.
    • Word, Excel, Pages, Keynote, CSV and more use the same previews as Finder's Quick Look.
    • Attached folders open as a list you can click into.
  • Always current. When your assistant edits a document you're reading, the view updates in place and keeps your scroll position.
  • Talk about it while you read. The message box stays under the document, and what you send refers to it. Select a passage and choose Quote in reply to quote it.
  • Get around quickly.
    • ⌃⌘← and ⌃⌘→ step through a message's attachments.
    • Links to local files inside a document open in the viewer.
    • ⌘F finds text.
    • New messages and questions show as jump buttons instead of pulling you away.
  • Safe by default. The viewer reads only the file you clicked and loads nothing from the internet. Apps and scripts are shown in Finder instead of being previewed.
  • Your assistant knows. The instructions Zeus writes for your assistant now say you read documents in Zeus, so it prefers Markdown, keeps the same file when it updates one, and says what changed. Restart Assistant picks them up if you haven't edited your copy.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.8
item.description:
• Choose your text size. Settings › Appearance has a new Text size control under Conversation font: Small, Default, Large or Larger. It sizes the conversation, the message box, the status line, the speech bubble and attachment chips. The pixel font stays sharp at every size.
  • Jump around the conversation, Slack-style. Small floating buttons now help you find your place:
    • ↑ N unread at the top takes you to the oldest message you haven't read. Its × marks them all as read.
    • ↓ N new or ↓ Latest at the bottom brings you back to the newest message when you've scrolled up.
    • ? Question appears when one of your assistant's questions is off screen, with an arrow pointing to it. Click again to step through open questions, together with the status line.
  • At narrow widths the buttons shrink to an arrow and a count.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.7
item.description:
• Rate what your assistant tells you. Hover a message your assistant sent on its own and click the rating button: More like this, Only when I need to know, or Stop these. A rating applies to that kind of message, such as on-call reminders or meeting prep notes, not just the one message. You can edit the kind's name, or choose Just this one. ⌘R rates the message in focus. Replies to your own messages aren't rated.
  • Stop means stop. Your assistant stops sending that kind, and Zeus holds any that still arrive, even ones marked urgent. Zeus also compares new messages with the kinds you stopped, using Apple's on-device language tools, to catch look-alikes sent under a different name. Held messages are never deleted: they collapse in the conversation with Show, each says why it was held, and Not this kind lets it through.
  • Only when I need to know asks your assistant to send that kind only when it matters to you.
  • What you hear about. A new list in Settings shows every kind you've rated, with an example, and lets you change or remove each one.
  • Your assistant learns your taste. Each rating goes to your assistant, which confirms it, and is saved in Zeus/preferences.md in its folder. The instructions Zeus writes for your assistant now ask it to name the kind of each message it sends on its own and to generalize from your ratings. Restart Assistant picks them up if you haven't edited your copy.
  • A nudge, never a mute. If you keep ignoring one kind of message, Zeus may ask whether you want to rate them. It never mutes anything on its own.
  • Attachments say what's in them. When your assistant shares a file or folder, it now has to include a short summary of what's inside and why it matters, and the message itself gives the takeaway. Zeus turns the message back until it does. A "have a look" with a bare file no longer gets through.
  • Quieter attachments. The large Open and Show in Finder buttons are gone. Each attachment is now a small chip with its icon, name and summary: click it to open, use the small magnifier to show it in Finder, or right-click for Open, Show in Finder and Copy Path. The instructions Zeus writes for your assistant explain this; Restart Assistant picks them up if you haven't edited your copy.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.6
item.description:
• Your assistant's folder is its memory. Everything Zeus keeps, after its privacy safeguards, is now also written as readable files in your assistant's folder under Zeus/: each day's activity, windows, screenshots with their descriptions, typing topics, summaries and moments, plus reflections and the current rules. It builds up whether or not anything was sent. Retention and deletion apply to the files too, and a file you delete in Finder stays deleted.
  • Summaries point to the files. Morning summaries, moments and reflections still go to your assistant as before, and each now ends with a line naming the files to look at.
  • Your assistant learns you. The instructions Zeus writes for a new assistant now explain the folder, ask the assistant to learn your habits and patterns, and give it a Notes/ folder for its own conclusions. If you haven't edited your copy, Restart Assistant refreshes it.
  • Cover pictures and faces. A new switch in Settings › Privacy, on by default. Turn it off for full trust and screenshots are kept as they are. Passwords, card numbers and keys are always covered. The separate Raw on request switches are gone: what your assistant can read follows the levels you turned on.
  • Show in Finder. Settings and What Zeus Kept show your assistant's folder and open any item or day in Finder. Delete Everything asks before deleting your assistant's own notes.
  • A new README and a full manual. The README leads with the learning story. New guides cover setup, assistants, the conversation, characters and themes, Learn from me, privacy, every setting, every tool your assistant can use, and troubleshooting.
  • Fixes. Restarting the assistant Zeus runs no longer takes extra recovery steps, so it's about twice as fast. Time-based rules from assistants that check tool schemas are no longer rejected. Rules, redaction and typing-consent wording now match what Zeus does.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.5
item.description:
• Summaries and notes now reach your assistant. The morning summary and the day's notes are delivered to your assistant the same way your messages are, and your assistant confirms each one. They queue if the assistant isn't connected yet and go to a restarted assistant on their own. Before, they were only announced quietly, and an assistant that never asked for them never saw them.
  • "Sent" means received. The conversation says "Daily summary ready for your assistant · View" until the assistant has it, then "Sent your daily summary". In What Zeus Kept, Sent to your assistant shows a Waiting group for anything prepared but not yet received, with the reason and the fix: Start Assistant, Open in Terminal, or Restart Assistant.
  • Stuck deliveries say so. If a message, summary or reflection has waited ten minutes because the assistant's Terminal has unsent text, or it's busy, or it isn't connected, a quiet line says which, with Open in Terminal, and Don't send for the one item. Zeus still never types over text you left in the Terminal.
  • New tools need a restart, and Zeus says so. When a Zeus update adds tools or instructions for your assistant, the conversation and Settings › Assistant show "Zeus has new tools and instructions · Restart assistant". The conversation is kept. If you haven't edited the instructions Zeus wrote for a new assistant, Zeus refreshes them on restart; if you have, it offers to open the folder or replace them, after asking.
  • Delete Everything also discards summaries and reflections still waiting to be delivered, and a late confirmation can't bring them back.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.4
item.description:
• Choice buttons answer on the first click. Clicking an option in a question used to move keyboard focus to it, and the thread then scrolled to centre that option while the mouse button was still down, so the click landed on nothing. The thread no longer scrolls for a focus change that came from the pointer; Tab, the arrow keys and the strip's jumps still reveal what they focus. The same goes for every click target in the conversation, and for the peek bubble's inline choices while it's still typing.
  • README and setup guide cover all of Learn from me. The four levels and the permission each needs, how private details are removed on your Mac (fixed patterns, Apple's data detectors and name tagging, the on-device Foundation Model, Vision for text and faces, nothing to any cloud), what your assistant gets, Raw on request, rules that act for you, Ask About This, What Zeus Kept and the Sent ledger.
  • Your assistant knows the newer tools. The assistant template Zeus writes for a new assistant now explains when to ask the journal, how shadow and hands-off rules report what they did, and that purchases always ask first.
  • Copy. The Screen level says "pixellated" everywhere, matching what Zeus does to pictures and faces. The apps-and-timing retention default reads 90 days, as it is.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.3
item.description:
• Level 4: Zeus can learn from what you type, privately. Settings › Privacy › Typing, off by default, per app. Zeus groups what you type into short runs, removes private details on your Mac, and turns each run into a one-line topic with Apple's on-device model ("drafting a reply about Thursday"). Password fields are never seen: macOS switches to secure input the moment one takes focus. Pasted text is marked as pasted and never read. Topics are kept for 30 days and the redacted words for 24 hours by default; "topics only" is one switch away. The menu says "Private input" while a password field has focus.
  • Your assistant can ask the journal. "What was I doing at three?" gets an answer from what Zeus kept: summaries, descriptions and topics, never pictures or words unless you turned on "Raw on request" for that level. Every answer shows in the conversation as "Looked at your journal · View" and in the Sent ledger, exactly as sent.
  • Rules that act for you. A rule that would do something first shows "I'd have … · OK next time? · Not this". One OK makes it hands-off, with "Did: … · Undo" each time; "Not this" retires it. Purchases always ask, every time, with the amount.
  • Rules learn from what you do. Accepting, undoing, skipping, ignoring, turning off and editing all move a rule's confidence; rules that stop working retire themselves and won't be proposed again for a month. "Why?" in Settings › Rules lists each outcome with its date.
  • What Zeus Kept shows typing grouped by app and hour, with the topic first and the redacted words beneath when kept; delete any run.
  • Journal when the keychain is locked. If Zeus starts while your keychain is unavailable, it keeps new records in memory, says so in Settings › Privacy, and saves them once you unlock.
  • Fixes. An idle connection listener no longer leaks; shadow lines read naturally; amounts show as money; the Privacy pane previews include every level.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.1
item.description:
• Only your assistant can talk to Zeus. Other agent sessions that happen to have the Zeus server configured are refused with a clear message and never reach your conversation. If one tries, Zeus shows at most one quiet line a day: "Another session tried to reach Zeus · Make it my assistant · Ignore". Settings › Assistant › "Who may talk to Zeus" switches back to "Any session" if you run several agents on purpose.
  • Level 3: Zeus can see your screen, privately. Settings › Privacy › Screen, off by default. When you switch apps or documents, every few minutes in the same place, or when you ask, Zeus takes a picture of the window in front and describes it on your Mac with Apple's on-device model. Text that looks private is blurred, pictures and faces are pixellated, and password dialogs, Keychain, banking apps, video calls, presentations and private browser windows are never captured. Pictures are kept for a week, descriptions for up to 90 days; everything is in What Zeus Kept.
  • Ask about this. Press Shift with your Talk shortcut in any app and the conversation opens with what you're looking at attached: the window, the file or page, and (with Screen Recording on) a picture, each a chip you can remove before sending.
  • Phase A polish. Settings and What Zeus Kept follow a fixed-appearance theme; dropped attachments are chips; the Privacy pane groups each level's controls; rule triggers read naturally; rule notices say "I'd have acted on…", "OK. I'll do that…" and "Got it. I won't."
  • Fixes. Receipts are kept for retry when writing history fails; "Pause for today" resumes on its own at the deadline.

item.title: Zeus 0.2.0
item.description:
• Drop anything on Zeus. Drag files, folders, text, images or links onto Zeus and the conversation opens with them attached, ready for your message. If Zeus runs your assistant, a dropped folder can become its working folder.
  • Zeus learns how you work, in levels. Settings › Privacy now has levels, each its own switch, off by default. Level 1 is what you had: apps and timing. Level 2, new, keeps the title of the window in front, the file it shows and the web address, so your assistant knows what you were working on. It needs Accessibility permission and shows an example of what it keeps before it starts. Pick "everywhere except my private list" or "only in apps I choose".
  • Private details are removed on your Mac before anything is kept. Names, emails, phone numbers, cards, addresses, passwords and keys are replaced with placeholders by fixed patterns and Apple's on-device model. Password fields, private browser windows, your private list and a locked screen are never recorded. Nothing raw leaves the Mac.
  • What Zeus Kept. See every record exactly as stored, redactions visible, and everything sent to your assistant. Delete one item, a day, an app, or everything. Records are encrypted on disk.
  • Rules. Once a day your assistant looks over a short summary of your day and suggests rules about how to help you. Rules about timing and tone start at once, with a quiet line in the conversation; rules that would act for you first show what they'd have done and wait for one OK. Settings › Rules shows every rule with its evidence, lets you edit, add or turn off, and has one dial from "Ask me first" to "Just do it". Rules that stop working retire themselves. Purchases always ask.
  • Zeus holds back when a rule says so. A rule like "hold routine messages after 18:00" keeps the badge and the thread but skips the pop-up and sound until the rule clears.

item.title: Zeus 0.1.11
item.description: • Pick any shortcut for Talk to Zeus. Settings › General now has a shortcut field: click it, press the keys you want, and that's the shortcut. Any key works, including function keys, arrows and Space; combinations macOS owns, or that another app already uses, are refused and the old shortcut stays. Delete clears it, the ↺ button restores the default ⌥⌘Z. Your current shortcut is kept.

item.title: Zeus 0.1.10
item.description:
• Terminal-pane sessions stop "thinking" on time too. If you connect your own assistant through its Terminal pane, Zeus now reads that pane (only while it's waiting on a reply, never typing into it) and ends the thinking indicator a few seconds after the turn ends, even without the launch hook.
  • Honest "off" state. After you stop the assistant Zeus runs, the menu and the status strip say "Your assistant is off" instead of "Ready to talk" and "Idle".
  • Sending from history. Sending a message while scrolled back in the conversation now returns you to the newest message.
  • Settings tabs for VoiceOver and automation. Each Settings tab now has a real name and reports when it's selected, so screen readers and UI scripting see "General", "Appearance", "Assistant", "Character", "Privacy" and "About".

item.title: Zeus 0.1.9
item.description:
• One menu. The menu bar icon and a right-click on Zeus now show the same menu: status (with a jump to the waiting question or unread message), Talk, Hide, Character, Size, Theme, Settings, Check for Updates, About, Quit.
  • Hide the menu bar icon. Settings › General › "Show menu bar icon". Zeus always stays reachable: turning the icon off shows Zeus, reopening the app brings Zeus back, and ⌥⌘Z keeps working.
  • Your assistant's own updates. When the assistant Zeus runs has an update waiting (Claude Code's "Restart to update"), one quiet line offers "Restart assistant". It restarts at a safe moment and keeps the conversation. Nothing restarts without your click.
  • Zeus knows the moment your assistant finishes. Sessions Zeus launches, and sessions you start with the command copied from Settings, now tell Zeus when a turn ends. The thinking indicator clears in well under a second even when the assistant doesn't send a reply, for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode. Nothing in your saved agent configuration is changed; the hook applies to that launch only.

item.title: Zeus 0.1.8
item.description:
• Your assistant can control Zeus. New tools let it switch or create characters and themes, move Zeus, change its size, hide it for a while, adjust look-and-feel settings, check for updates and install one after announcing it. Every change shows in the conversation as one line with Undo. It can never answer its own questions, change its own permissions or session, or touch your data. Two switches in Settings › General: "Let my assistant control Zeus" and "Let my assistant install updates" (both on).
  • Status strip. A line between the messages and the input tells you why Zeus shows "?" or "!" and takes you to that message. Skip a question you don't want to answer (your assistant is told). Quick buttons: Terminal, New conversation, Clear, Settings. ⌘J jumps. Clicking Zeus while it shows "?" opens the conversation at that question.
  • Learn from me (off by default). Settings › Privacy: Zeus can note when and in which apps you work, on this Mac only, and send your assistant a short morning summary plus up to four notes a day. No keystrokes, window titles or screenshots. Private apps count as private time with no name. See what was recorded, pause for today, or delete everything.
  • Keyboard and VoiceOver. Every new control has one Tab stop and a themed focus ring. ⌘⌥← and ⌘⌥→ change the panel width; Reset width is in the panel's menu. Undo and the private-app picker announce their results.
  • Links are clickable. Web, file and mail addresses in messages open with a click.
  • Connect your own. Switching away from "Zeus runs it" while the agent is running now asks "Stop the Zeus-run agent?" with Stop or Keep Running.
  • Zeus stops "thinking" when the agent is done. When the assistant Zeus runs finishes its turn without sending a reply, the thinking indicator and pose now end as soon as its terminal goes idle, instead of after five minutes.
  • Fade works even with a question waiting. "Fade Zeus when idle" now dims Zeus after the delay even while a question is open or the assistant is working. A new question or new work brings Zeus back, then it fades again.
  • Typed answers close option questions. When your assistant asks a question with choices and you type your answer instead of clicking one, the question is answered with your text instead of staying open with a "?" over Zeus.
  • Terminal prompts that vanish. If an assistant prompt disappears from Terminal without Zeus seeing the answer, the prompt card closes as unconfirmed after 30 seconds instead of staying open.

item.title: Zeus 0.1.7
item.description:
• Themes. Settings › Appearance has seven themes for the conversation, speech bubble and Settings (Classic, Midnight, Parchment, Olympus, Phosphor, Pocket, Sorbet). Import your own as a JSON file; Open Example shows how.
  • Import a character. Settings › Character gets Import Character…, Open Example and Open Characters Folder. New or edited character files load without restarting Zeus, and a bad file says exactly what's wrong.
  • Ghost mode. Settings › Character › "Fade Zeus when idle": pick an opacity and a delay. Zeus comes back when you point at it, press the shortcut, or something arrives.
  • Resizable conversation. Drag the panel's edge to make it wider; Zeus remembers the width.
  • Settings changes apply to the running assistant. Changing the permission mode or instructions restarts the assistant in the same conversation at a safe moment. Changing the agent or folder asks before switching.
  • Settings window is resizable and General has a jump row to its sections.
  • Unsent text in Terminal. If your own typed text is sitting in the assistant's terminal, Zeus now tells you why messages are waiting, with Open in Terminal and Cancel queued messages. Zeus never clears or sends your draft.

item.title: Zeus 0.1.6
item.description:
• Answer your assistant's questions in the chat. When Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode asks for permission, Zeus shows the question with the agent's own choices as buttons. Click one and Zeus presses exactly that choice. It never answers on its own.
  • Line breaks come through. Shift+Return starts a new line, and your assistant receives the message exactly as you wrote it.
  • Pop-up sound. Turn it on in Settings › General › Sounds and pick the Zeus chime or a macOS sound.

item.title: Zeus 0.1.5
item.description:
Zeus now keeps itself up to date.

  • Check for Updates… in the menu bar menu, and a daily automatic check you can turn off in Settings › General.
  • Settings › General shows the version you're running.
  • The message box grows as you type, up to six lines.
  • Settings shows the terminal command as tmux attach -t zeus.
